hints: Apply the SUVAT equation $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$ (or $v^2 = u^2 - 2ds$ where $d$ is deceleration) separately to sections $AB$ and $BC$.
For section $AB$, with speeds from $20\text{ m s}^{-1}$ to $12\text{ m s}^{-1}$: $12^2 = 20^2 - 2d(AB) \implies 2d(AB) = 400 - 144 = 256$.
For section $BC$, with speeds from $12\text{ m s}^{-1}$ to $6\text{ m s}^{-1}$: $6^2 = 12^2 - 2d(BC) \implies 2d(BC) = 144 - 36 = 108$.
Divide the two equations to eliminate the common factor $2d$: $\frac{AB}{BC} = \frac{256}{108}$, then divide numerator and denominator by $4$.
walkthrough:
Name the foundational SUVAT relation between initial speed $u$, final speed $v$, deceleration $d$, and distance $s$:
$$v^2 = u^2 - 2ds$$

Consider section $AB$. Here the particle enters with speed $u = 20\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and leaves with speed $v = 12\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$12^2 = 20^2 - 2d(AB)$$

Rearrange to express $AB$ in terms of $d$:
$$2d(AB) = 400 - 144 = 256 \implies AB = \frac{256}{2d} = \frac{128}{d} \quad \text{--- (Equation 1)}$$

Now consider section $BC$. The particle enters with speed $u = 12\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and leaves with speed $v = 6\text{ m s}^{-1}$ under the same deceleration $d$:
$$6^2 = 12^2 - 2d(BC)$$

Rearrange to express $BC$ in terms of $d$:
$$2d(BC) = 144 - 36 = 108 \implies BC = \frac{108}{2d} = \frac{54}{d} \quad \text{--- (Equation 2)}$$

Divide Equation 1 by Equation 2 to find the ratio $AB:BC$:
$$\frac{AB}{BC} = \frac{128/d}{54/d} = \frac{128}{54}$$
Divide both numerator and denominator by $2$ to simplify to lowest terms:
$$\frac{128}{54} = \frac{64}{27} \implies AB:BC = 64:27$$

hints: The particle comes to rest at $D$ ($v = 0$); use the motion across the entire interval $AD$ where $u = 20\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $s = 80\text{ m}$.
Apply $v^2 = u^2 - 2ds$ to $AD$: $0 = 20^2 - 2d(80)$ to determine the numerical deceleration $d$.
Substitute this value of $d$ into $BC = \frac{54}{d}$ from part (i) to find the distance $BC$.
walkthrough: Identify the motion across section $AD$: the particle starts at $A$ with initial speed $u = 20\text{ m s}^{-1}$, comes to rest at $D$ with $v = 0\text{ m s}^{-1}$, and travels distance $AD = 80\text{ m}$.

Apply the formula $v^2 = u^2 - 2ds$ to the section $AD$:
$$0^2 = 20^2 - 2 \times d \times 80$$

Add $160d$ to both sides and divide by $160$ to solve for the deceleration $d$:
$$160d = 400 \implies d = \frac{400}{160} = \frac{40}{16} = 2.5\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Recall from part (i) the formula for the distance of section $BC$:
$$BC = \frac{54}{d}$$

Substitute $d = 2.5\text{ m s}^{-2}$ into this expression:
$$BC = \frac{54}{2.5} = \frac{54 \times 4}{10} = \frac{216}{10} = 21.6\text{ m}$$
